Vs

full_judgment: 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned Appellate Court during disposal of the appeal committed material illegality and irregularity in deciding the merit of the suit against the plaintiff-petitioner and in favour of the defendant-opposite parties. There has been misreading and non-reading of evidence in sifting evidence and the learned lower appellate court has totally failed to assess the evidence on records and appreciate the actual position of law. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the onus of proving that the domicile has been chosen in substitution for domicile of origin lies upon those who assert that the domicile of origin has been lost but the defendant-opposite parties could not proved that the plaintiff-petitioner ever became an Indian Citizen in substitution of his domicile of origin and as such under proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law despite the learned trial court rightly decreed the suit the court of appeal without considering the aforesaid aspect erred in law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The teamed Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner Mr. P.C. Guha also submits that the plaintiff-petitioner is a citizen of Bangladesh by birth and he never migrated to India with any intention to become a citizen them or he did no act subversive of the State and discipline. The defendant-opposite parties totally failed to show any scrap of paper or evidence that the plaintiff-petitioner has voluntarily renounced his original citizenship or guilty of some conducts as not being qualified to be deemed citizen of Bangladesh as per P.O. 149 of 1972 and as such the teamed lower appellate court was manifestly wrong in not dismissing the appeal with the holding that the defendant failed to prove that the plaintiff-petitioner has lost or renounced his citizenship by birth. Mr. Guha, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner further submits that the plaintiff-petitioner having not acquired the citizenship of any other country his citizenship of Bangladesh which he acquired by birth cannot be evaporated and he continues to be a citizen of Bangladesh and as such the learned trial court rightly decreed the suit holding that the plaintiff is entitled to get relief as prayed for. The learned counsel further submits that the domicile of origin is not a matter of choice or free will which is received or communicated to him by birth and the domicile in origin is not lost by mere absence for the time being nor it is extinguished for temporary absence of anybody. It is a fact that the plaintiff-petitioner was not present for the time being in this country (the then East Pakistan). But the temporary absence of the plaintiff for a particular period does not diver him from getting his right in holding citizenship of Bangladesh. The learned counsel for the petitioner lastly submits that in the year 1953 the plaintiff-petitioner never went to India after selling his landed properties rather he read upto class 7(seven) in this country under Police Station Kotalipara of Gopalganj District. In the year 1961 his name has been duly recorded in S.A. Khatian and the lands are still under his possession along with his co-sharers and the defendant-opposite parties although alleged that the plaintiff-petitioner and his elder brother after disposing the lands in the year 1953 migrated to India but has been hopelessly failed to prove that allegation. The plaintiff's land along with his homestead is found to be recorded in S.A. Khatian in his name along with his co-sharers but the court of appeal upon misreading of evidence illegally held that in 1953 the plaintiff-petitioner after the death of his father selling his all landed properties went to India. In G.R. case No. 192 of 1979 it was held by the learned Sub-divisional Magistrate of Goalanda on 19.12.1980 that the plaintiff-petitioner as a citizen of Bangladesh went to India and returned back to Bangladesh without valid document and though it is a verdict of a competent court of law that the plaintiff-petitioner is a citizen of Bangladesh the learned lower appellate court without considering the said facts upon misinterpreted Section 3(2) and (4) of Bangladesh (Control and Entry) Act, 1952 and that the trial court after proper consideration of the facts of the case and points of law involved therein rightly held that the post of Munsif is permanent and the appointment of the petitioner was on adhoc basis and the post of the plaintiff-petitioner being not temporary in nature he is protected under Article 135(2) of the Constitution of Bangladesh but the learned lower appellate court out of wrong assumption and wrong interpretation of law illegally held that the post of the petitioner was temporary which was terminable without show cause notice. The learned lower appellate court without reversing the findings of the trial court reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court illegally in violation of the provisions of Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and in view of the facts and circumstances of the case the impugned judgment and dismissal decree of the learned lower appellate court is not a proper judgment of reversal which deserve interference of this court.
